description: High-altitude birthplace-of-coffee terroir; washed coffees are floral and citric, naturals intensely fruited.
Southern zone neighboring Yirgacheffe; syrupy stone fruit and bergamot, both washed and natural processing.
Andean department with year-round micro-harvests; balanced, sweet, red-fruit-and-caramel profiles.
Central highlands; SL28/SL34 factories producing blackcurrant-driven, intensely juicy washed lots.
Remote non-volcanic highlands; dense, chocolate-and-stone-fruit washed coffees at serious altitude.
Flat, mechanized savanna plateau; nutty, chocolatey naturals that anchor espresso blends.
Steep valleys south of San José; honey-process pioneers with crisp, sugar-cane sweetness.
Volcanic slopes of Volcán Barú; home of hyper-aromatic Geisha lots and misty microclimates.
